title.narrative: Increased nutrition security by professionalisation of the cassava value chain

description.narrative: This Impact Cluster aims to professionalise Mozambique’s cassava value chain and strengthen nutrition security by introducing proven Dutch technologies, digital tools and standards into a fragile but highly promising sector. Cassava is Mozambique’s main staple, yet productivity is low, processing is largely artisanal, and industrial capacity is constrained by technological bottlenecks.The consortium combines complementary expertise: JK Techniek and TOP (NL) bring engineering solutions to resolve Dadtco Mandioca Mocambique LDA's (DMM’s) drying bottleneck (tripling capacity from 450 to 1,500 kg/hour) and valorise cassava by-products into animal feed. SmartFarming introduces open-source digital farmer registration and monitoring systems, enabling traceability and certification readiness. Instituto De Investigacão Agrária De Mocambique (IIAM) and Eduardo Mondlane (UEM) contribute cassava variety screening, multiplication, and the development of national starch product and process standards, while Casmara (SA) ensures market linkage and certification for South African buyers. DMM, Mozambique’s only industrial cassava processor, anchors the project locally and integrates 200 lead farmers, 4,000 smallholders and artisanal rale producers into its supply chain.The project delivers direct results across the value chain:• Improved availability of high-yielding, disease-resistant cassava varieties and farmer training increase smallholder productivity by 30%+.• Professionalisation and market linkage of artisanal rale producers raise daily output from ~150 kg/day to ~1,000 kg/day.• Digitalisation enables performance monitoring of over 4,200 farmers.• DMM achieves structural profitability and prepares investment in a second mobile production line (~€1.5m).• National starch standards and FSSC22000 certification position Mozambique’s cassava industry to compete with Asian imports.Expected impacts include: 225+ new jobs in farming, processing and services; higher and more stable incomes for 4,200 farmers; certified, safe and affordable cassava products for local and regional markets; and stronger nutrition security through diversified diets (rale and animal feed). The project creates a scalable business case that can be replicated in other cassava-rich regions, directly contributing to SDG8 and on private sector development and food security.
